editorial.marketOverview: US equities enter Monday after a historic Friday liquidation, with Nasdaq and semiconductor shares disproportionately weak. Monday futures point to a significant relief bounce, but the underlying three-day risk remains elevated until cash-market breadth and semiconductor leadership confirm. Taiwan's stabilization contrasts with persistent Korean weakness.
editorial.whatChanged: Fresh FT Monday coverage puts Nasdaq-100 futures at +2.8% and S&P futures at +2.1%, broadly confirming the previously reported near-3% futures rebound. Taiwan's TSMC gained about 2% while South Korean chipmakers remained under pressure. Reuters' updated Brent and WTI indications are slightly positive. These refine the cross-market picture without a new regime change.
editorial.marketInterpretation: A sharp futures rebound after forced selling can be short-covering rather than durable demand. Friday's SOX underperformance and weak breadth remain the most important verified US cash evidence. A constructive reassessment requires QQQ and SOX/SMH moving together with better breadth and easing VXN/VIX. Treasury curve, FedWatch and current volatility are not verified; the older 29 bp spread is stale, not current.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday: relief-rally potential is high, but watch whether the cash session holds its opening gains and whether chips participate. Tuesday: consumer confidence and Dell's AI-infrastructure commentary can either support or challenge the rebound. Wednesday: PCE, GDP and Beige Book can reset rate expectations and produce outsized volatility before the holiday closure.
editorial.bullCase: QQQ and SOX sustain Monday gains into the close, market breadth improves and volatility falls. Dell's results support demand and Wednesday inflation does not force a hawkish repricing. This would challenge the bearish three-day baseline.
editorial.bearCase: Monday's rebound fades, SOX/SMH lag QQQ and market breadth remains poor. Additional AI financing or regulatory worries and a hotter inflation surprise would revive liquidation pressure; oil-related geopolitical risk may amplify it.
editorial.watchNext: Verify Monday 09:45 EST flash PMIs, cash-session QQQ/SOX/SMH leadership, advance-decline breadth, synchronized VXN/VIX and paired 2Y/10Y yields. Tuesday consumer confidence and Dell earnings; Wednesday 08:30 EST PCE/GDP and 14:00 EST Beige Book. Do not infer US cash response from futures or regional markets.
